content_voiceover: This slide lists the International Consensus Classification's genetically-defined AML subtypes, which still require a 20% blast threshold, unlike the 10% cutoff used for a subset marked in red on this slide. Acute promyelocytic leukemia with the t 15;17 translocation and PML-RARA fusion tops the list, since it's a hematologic emergency treated without conventional chemotherapy. Other core-binding factor and recurrent translocations follow: t 8;21 with RUNX1-RUNX1T1, inversion 16 with CBFB-MYH11, t 9;11 with MLLT3-KMT2A and other KMT2A rearrangements, t 6;9 with DEK-NUP214, inversion 3 with GATA2 and MECOM, and t 9;22 with BCR-ABL1, which requires distinguishing de novo AML from blast-phase CML. Mutation-defined entities include AML with mutated NPM1, in-frame bZIP CEBPA mutations, and AML with mutated TP53, which requires a single mutation with variant allele frequency over 10% and uses the lower 10% blast threshold. Know that APL and BCR-ABL1 positive AML are the two subtypes where you must actively exclude alternative diagnoses, promyelocytic variants or CML blast crisis, respectively.
keypoints: t(9;22) BCR-ABL1: exclude CML blast phase
TP53mut AML: single mutation, VAF>10%, blast>=10%
keypoint_voiceover: APL is the must-recognize emergency here. TP53-mutated AML uses a lower 10% blast cutoff in ICC, while everything else still needs 20%.
